questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If a circuit has zero reactance, it is possible that the circuit contains
options: both an inductor and a capacitor
neither an inductor nor a capacitor
questions.solution:
The net reactance of an AC circuit is given by $X = X_L - X_C = \omega L - \dfrac{1}{\omega C}$.

For the circuit to have zero reactance, $X = 0$, which requires $X_L = X_C$.

This condition can be satisfied in two cases:

First, if the circuit contains neither an inductor nor a capacitor. In this case, $X_L = 0$ and $X_C = 0$, making the net reactance zero. This corresponds to a purely resistive circuit.

Second, if the circuit contains both an inductor and a capacitor. At the resonant frequency, the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance ($X_L = X_C$), and they cancel each other out, making the net reactance zero.

If the circuit contains only an inductor or only a capacitor, the net reactance will be non-zero (assuming a non-zero frequency).

Therefore, it is possible that the circuit contains both an inductor and a capacitor, or neither of them.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An inductor-coil possessing some resistance is connected to an AC source. Which of the following quantities exhibit a zero average value over one complete cycle?
options: Magnetic energy stored in the inductor
questions.solution:
For an AC circuit, the current is given by $I = I_0 \sin(\omega t - \phi)$.

The average value of current over one complete cycle is $\langle I \rangle = \dfrac{1}{T} \int_0^T I_0 \sin(\omega t - \phi) dt = 0$.

The Joule heat dissipated per unit time is $P = I^2 R = I_0^2 R \sin^2(\omega t - \phi)$. Its average value over one cycle is $\langle P \rangle = \dfrac{1}{2} I_0^2 R \neq 0$.

The magnetic energy stored in the inductor is $U = \dfrac{1}{2} L I^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} L I_0^2 \sin^2(\omega t - \phi)$. Its average value over one cycle is $\langle U \rangle = \dfrac{1}{4} L I_0^2 \neq 0$.

The induced emf in the inductor is $e = -L \dfrac{dI}{dt} = -L I_0 \omega \cos(\omega t - \phi)$. Its average value over one complete cycle is $\langle e \rangle = \dfrac{1}{T} \int_0^T -L I_0 \omega \cos(\omega t - \phi) dt = 0$.

Therefore, the current and the induced emf exhibit a zero average value over one complete cycle.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following instruments can be used to measure the AC voltage across a resistance?
questions.solution:
An alternating current (AC) reverses its direction periodically. The average value of AC over a complete cycle is zero.

Instruments like the moving-coil galvanometer, moving-magnet galvanometer, and potentiometer measure the average value of voltage or current. If connected to an AC circuit, their pointers will not deflect because the average AC voltage is zero.

A hot-wire voltmeter works on the principle of the heating effect of electric current, given by $H = \dfrac{V^2}{R}t$. Since the heat produced is proportional to the square of the voltage, it is independent of the direction of the current. Therefore, a hot-wire voltmeter can measure both AC and DC voltages, specifically measuring the root-mean-square (RMS) value of the AC voltage.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following devices can be employed to convert mechanical energy into electrical energy?
questions.solution:
A dynamo is a device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy based on the principle of electromagnetic induction.

Both AC dynamo and DC dynamo are types of generators that perform this conversion.

A motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy.

A transformer transfers electrical energy between circuits and does not convert mechanical energy into electrical energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For an AC series circuit, the instantaneous current becomes zero at the moment the instantaneous voltage reaches its maximum value. The components connected to the source could be a
options: combination of an inductor and a capacitor
questions.solution:
Let the instantaneous voltage be $V = V_{0} \cos(\omega t)$. The voltage reaches its maximum value at $t = 0$.

Let the instantaneous current be $I = I_{0} \cos(\omega t + \phi)$, where $\phi$ is the phase difference between the voltage and the current.

Given that at $t = 0$, $I = 0$.

Substituting $t = 0$ in the current equation:

$I_{0} \cos(\phi) = 0 \Rightarrow \cos(\phi) = 0 \Rightarrow \phi = \pm \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

The phase difference between the voltage and the current is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. This means the circuit is purely reactive and has zero resistance ($R = 0$).

This condition is satisfied by:
1. A pure capacitor (current leads voltage by $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$)
2. A pure inductor (current lags voltage by $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$)
3. A series combination of an inductor and a capacitor (net reactance is either purely inductive or purely capacitive, so the phase difference remains $\pm \dfrac{\pi}{2}$)

A pure resistor has a phase difference of $0$, so it does not satisfy the condition.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An inductor, a resistor, and a capacitor are connected in series with an AC source. When the frequency of the source is slightly increased from a very low initial value, the reactance
questions.solution:
The reactance of an inductor is given by $X_L = \omega L = 2\pi f L$, where $f$ is the frequency of the AC source.

When the frequency $f$ is increased, the inductive reactance $X_L$ increases.

The reactance of a capacitor is given by $X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi f C}$.

When the frequency $f$ is increased, the capacitive reactance $X_C$ decreases.

The resistance $R$ of a resistor is independent of the frequency of the AC source.

At very low frequencies, the circuit is highly capacitive ($X_C > X_L$). The magnitude of the net reactance of the circuit is $|X| = X_C - X_L$, which decreases as the frequency increases towards the resonant frequency.

Therefore, only the reactance of the inductor increases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circuit is supplied with a current of $10 \text{ A}$ (rms) by an AC source rated at $100 \text{ V}$ (rms). The average power delivered by the source
questions.solution:
The average power delivered by an AC source is given by $P_{avg} = V_{rms} I_{rms} \cos \phi$, where $\cos \phi$ is the power factor of the circuit.

Given $V_{rms} = 100 \text{ V}$ and $I_{rms} = 10 \text{ A}$, we have $P_{avg} = 100 \times 10 \times \cos \phi = 1000 \cos \phi \text{ W}$.

Since the power factor $\cos \phi$ satisfies $0 \le \cos \phi \le 1$ for any passive circuit, the maximum possible average power is $1000 \text{ W}$ (when $\cos \phi = 1$, for a purely resistive circuit).

For circuits containing inductive or capacitive elements, $\cos \phi < 1$, so the average power will be less than $1000 \text{ W}$.

Thus, the average power can be exactly $1000 \text{ W}$ or less than $1000 \text{ W}$.
